statement: For $x\\ge0$, the function $f(x)=\\dfrac{x}{1+x^{2}}$ has a maximum. Find the value of $x$ at which it occurs and the maximum value. Show also that $f$ is an odd function.
solution: $f'(x)=\\dfrac{(1+x^{2})-x(2x)}{(1+x^{2})^{2}}=\\dfrac{1-x^{2}}{(1+x^{2})^{2}}$. For $x\\ge0$ the only critical point is $x=1$; $f'(x)>0$ for $0<x<1$ and $f'(x)<0$ for $x>1$, so the maximum occurs at $x=1$ with value $f(1)=\\tfrac12$. Finally $f(-x)=\\frac{-x}{1+(-x)^{2}}=-\\frac{x}{1+x^{2}}=-f(x)$, so $f$ is odd.
